transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood CSM) — Anika (Procurement), David (Legal), Maya (Eng), Tom (Security)

Summary (auto):
- Procurement and legal kick-off for Redwood vendor onboarding for Velox Health. Focus on MSA redlines, DPA clauses, SLA/performance appendix, pricing approval flow, SOC2/KMS and onboarding checklist.
- Agreement to circulate redlines and SLA appendix; procurement will route pricing through internal finance approvers. Security team requested KMS and data residency confirmation for PHI.

Topics:
- MSA redline items: liability, indemnity, termination for convenience, data ownership
- DPA and data processing for healthcare PHI: encryption, KMS, audit logs, data residency
- SLA metrics: latency p95, availability, credits, support response times
- Pricing approval path: procurement, finance approvers, target start date for dedicated capacity pilot
- Vendor onboarding tasks and timelines

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. We have about 45 minutes, just want to run through where we are on the contract and pricing approvals and make sure we capture next steps with procurement and legal. 
[00:12] Anika: Thanks Jordan. We do want to be efficient — procurement needs the MSA with redlines and a copy of the DPA. Our finance team wants to see the pricing sheet and the expected monthly burn for the pilot.
[00:23] Priya: Totally. We have a draft SLA appendix that lays out p95, availability targets, support tiers. I'll pull the benchmark numbers — they were run on a 16A GPU pool for the model family you tested.
[00:36] David: Quick ask from legal: indemnity cap, limitation of liability, and termination for convenience — are these negotiable?
[00:42] Jordan: Yes, those are the usual redlines. From Redwood's perspective, we try to keep liability caps tied to fees paid, request mutual indemnity where possible, and carve-outs for gross negligence. But happy to redline specifically for Velox.
[00:57] David: Okay, our standard asks are higher cap for IP claims and indemnity around PHI misuse.
[01:06] Tom: On the security side — since Velox handles PHI, we need to confirm encryption at rest with customer-managed keys, KMS integration, audit logs accessible for X months, and where data is stored for residency.
[01:18] Priya: We support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; for Hosted we can offer VPC peering and region controls. Audit logs are part of the console — we can export logs to your SIEM. I will share the security checklist and our SOC 2 report.
[01:32] Maya: For the pilot, we prefer a dedicated capacity slice to reduce noisy neighbor and maintain latency. Is there a separate onboarding sequence for Dedicated?
[01:40] Marco: Yes, dedicated has a vendor onboarding flow — provisioning, networking (VPC), and test harness. We'll provide a checklist — it typically takes 2–3 weeks depending on approvals.
[01:50] Anika: Procurement will need the onboarding checklist to estimate lead time and commit windows to stakeholders. Also need the exact pricing tiers broken out: hosted per-token, embeddings, and dedicated monthly commit.
[02:05] Jordan: We'll send a pricing pack. One thing to call out: for Dedicated we typically have an upfront committed monthly charge with overage billing. We can include a pilot pricing line that scales.
[02:18] David: Back to the MSA: our legal team wants data ownership explicitly stated: customer retains all customer data; vendor gets a license to process for the service.
[02:29] Jordan: That's standard; our default MSA has a data processing clause and DPA. I'll redline to make customer ownership explicit.
[02:35] David: And what about breach notification timelines and SOC 2 evidence? We may need quarterly attestations or at least the report plus an executive summary.
[02:45] Priya: We can provide SOC 2 Type II report and an executive summary. For breaches, Redwood commits to notify within 72 hours per the DPA. We can discuss tighter windows but 72 is our default.
[02:58] Tom: Can we get more detail on key rotation and encryption algorithms used for in-flight and at-rest? Also whether HSM-backed keys are available.
[03:08] Priya: We use industry standard TLS1.2/1.3 in transit and AES-256 at rest. HSM-backed customer-managed KMS can be supported for Private installs; for Hosted we can integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping in certain regions. I'll include the security doc with exact cipher suites and key rotation cadence.
[03:25] Anika: Great. On pricing approvals — our process is: procurement sends package to finance, finance runs a TCO worksheet, then execs sign off. Typical cycle is 7–10 business days if nothing tricky. We need to know expected monthly cost of the pilot.
[03:39] Jordan: Understood. We'll provide a projected monthly burn based on the traffic estimates you gave in the discovery (about 40M tokens / month), and a pilot price for a 3-week test on a dedicated slice.
[03:52] Maya: A clarifying question — what happens if during the pilot we exceed token estimates? Do we have autoscale or will performance degrade?
[04:01] Priya: For Dedicated we can configure burst capacity and autoscale policies; we'll include guidance on expected latency as load increases and also the overage pricing rules.
[04:12] David: From legal perspective, we also need to confirm subcontractors and third-party processors — who will have access to data and what controls are in place.
[04:21] Jordan: We will include a third-party processor list in the DPA appendix. Redwood's infra providers are named and we can provide SOC2 of those providers where available.
[04:33] Tom: On the audit logs, what retention do you offer out of the box? We might need 12 months for investigation purposes.
[04:40] Priya: Default is 90 days in the console, but we can configure exports to S3 or to your SIEM for longer retention. We'll note options in the security checklist.
[04:52] Anika: Who will be our point of contact during procurement and thus who will route the contract?
[04:58] Marco: I'm your onboarding CSM — I'll coordinate with procurement and make sure the ticketing and network details are available. Jordan will handle legal pricing threads. Priya will be the technical contact for the SLA and security questions.
[05:10] Jordan: I'll capture next steps now. I'll send an MSA redline and the pricing pack. Priya will follow up with the SLA appendix and the perf spreadsheet. Marco will open the vendor onboarding ticket.
[05:23] David: Quick callout — indemnity cap: can you provide two options? One tied to fees (12 months of fees) and another flat cap for IP claims? We want options to present internally.
[05:34] Jordan: Yes, we can provide both options in the redline so you have negotiation room.
[05:39] Maya: For the pilot timeline, our engineering team needs about a week to validate connectivity after provisioning. So factoring that in, we're looking to go live with the pilot in mid-July if approvals move quickly.
[05:51] Marco: That aligns with the 2–3 week onboarding once approvals are done — so target mid-July is reasonable.
[06:00] Anika: On procurement approvals, we'll need the business justification memo. Jordan, can you provide a 1‑pager summarizing the use case and expected ROI?
[06:11] Jordan: Yes, I'll include a short business case in the pricing pack.
[06:16] Tom: For compliance, one more technical ask — can Redwood support an isolated dedicated private deployment within our VPC? That would help with PHI controls.
[06:26] Priya: Yes, we can discuss Private deployment; for fully air-gapped on-prem we'd move to the Private product offering. There's some extra setup and licensing. I'll note the differences and the checklist.
[06:40] David: Regarding DPA, we need a data breach insurance clause and clarity about liability if Redwood is compromised.
[06:48] Jordan: We'll propose language consistent with our enterprise terms — we can add a cyber insurance clause and indicate limits. We'll send the redline for your counsel to review.
[06:58] Anika: For the pilot approval I should get the pricing sheet and onboarding checklist to attach to the formal procurement request by Monday. Is that feasible?
[07:07] Jordan: Yes — Priya will send the SLA appendix by Thursday, Jordan will send redline by Friday — hmm earlier we said dates in the next steps; let's reconfirm.
[07:18] Priya: I'll aim for 2025-06-19 for the SLA appendix and perf numbers. Jordan will aim for 2025-06-20 for MSA redline. Marco will open the ticket 2025-06-21.
[07:30] David: Good. One administrative item — please provide a vendor legal contact email for Lincoln & Partners (our vendor system) so we can route documents programmatically.
[07:38] Marco: I'll provide the vendor legal email and main contact.
[07:42] Jordan: Any other blockers?
[07:45] Maya: Only that the engineering security team wants the ability to run a small stress test pre-production to validate p95 under expected load — is that okay?
[07:55] Priya: Absolutely. We'll set up a staging endpoint and provide a test harness with scripts. We'll also provide expected metrics to compare.
[08:05] Anika: Perfect. If we get the documents this week, procurement can hit the finance route next week and hopefully approve the pilot before the end of the month.
[08:15] Jordan: Great. I'll recap next steps at the end.

Recap / Next steps (verbal):
- Jordan to send MSA redline with two indemnity options, business case 1‑pager, and vendor legal contact — due 2025-06-20.
- Priya to share SLA appendix, perf benchmarks, security checklist, SOC2 summary — due 2025-06-19.
- Marco to open vendor onboarding ticket, share onboarding checklist and vendor setup link — due 2025-06-21.
- David to confirm indemnity threshold preference and return comments to Jordan — target 2025-06-25.

Action items (auto):
- Jordan: prepare MSA redline and pricing pack
- Priya: SLA appendix, perf numbers, security docs
- Marco: onboarding ticket and vendor setup

End of call.
